recap.text:
GitHub 101 - Event Recap

GitHub 101, hosted by the GitHub Community Club (GCC), was a hands-on workshop designed to introduce participants to Git, GitHub, and their role in the modern developer ecosystem.

The session began with an introduction to the importance of GitHub in the developer community, its impact on collaboration and open-source development, and the key differences between Git and GitHub. Participants then moved into a practical walkthrough of the Git workflow, where they configured their Git usernames and email addresses, created and cloned repositories, added files, staged changes, committed their work, and pushed their first commits to GitHub.

Beyond the fundamentals, the workshop explored the evolving GitHub developer ecosystem through insights from GitHub's Octoverse report and emerging trends in software development, including the growing adoption of TypeScript and its recent rise in popularity.

The event concluded with an interactive quiz that tested participants' understanding of the session. With enthusiastic participation and plenty of engaging responses, the quiz added a competitive edge to the workshop, with goodies awarded to the top three winners.

Overall, GitHub 101 combined practical learning, community insights, and friendly competition, giving participants a stronger foundation in Git and GitHub and encouraging them to take their next steps as developers and contributors to the open-source community.
